% A caption inside a float's center group is the float's caption: LaTeX's
% own manual spells the figure idiom this way, and the table twin puts the
% caption after \end{tabular} inside the group. Synthetic: invented text,
% nothing from any private document.
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}

\section{Grouped floats}

A paragraph before the floats, so their separation is on the page.

\begin{figure}[h]
\begin{center}
An invented stand-in for a centred panel body.
\caption{An invented centred panel.}
\label{fig:panel}
\end{center}
\end{figure}

\begin{table}[h]
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
alpha & beta \\
gamma & delta \\
\end{tabular}
\caption{An invented centred strip.}
\label{tab:strip}
\end{center}
\end{table}

Figure~\ref{fig:panel} and Table~\ref{tab:strip} are referenced by the
numbers their captions carry.

\end{document}
